sections.html:
Two counters serve Catoosa County. The tax commissioner has an office at 796 LaFayette Street in Ringgold and another at 205 Forrest Road in Fort Oglethorpe, and both answer at (706) 965-2571.

Ringgold keeps an irregular schedule: doors open at 7:30 on Tuesdays, close at 6:00 on Thursdays, and run 8:30 to 5:00 the other three weekdays. Fort Oglethorpe is open 8:30 to 5:00 every weekday, with title work ending at 4:45 (5:45 on Thursdays).

Values are set by the Catoosa County Tax Assessor, 798 Lafayette Street, phone 706-965-3772. That office maintains over 28,000 real estate parcels and about 6,900 personal property and mobile home accounts. Its field appraisers show photo identification and drive marked county vehicles.

sections.h2: The December 20 bill and your taxing district
sections.html:
County taxes are generally due by December 20, and the one statement also carries the levies of the City of Ringgold and the City of Fort Oglethorpe. The district code on your bill tells you which jurisdiction applies.

Catoosa County taxing districts
District codeArea it covers
01Unincorporated county
02City of Ringgold
03City of Fort Oglethorpe

Voting districts do not line up with taxing districts, so go by the code printed on the bill. The tax commissioner's bill guide explains every column, and three are worth knowing before you sell.

  • Due date: the last day to pay with no chance of interest or penalty.
  • Sales tax credit: savings tied to the prior year's local option sales tax proceeds.
  • Notice of Assessment: an estimate, not a bill, and it may leave out exemptions you hold.

Mobile and manufactured homes in the county on January 1 are taxed by April 1 with a location permit. Missing that date adds a 10% penalty, a FiFa and a possible sale of the home.

File within 45 days of the date the notice was mailed. There are three ways to do it: in person at 798 Lafayette Street, by mail to the Tax Assessor at that address (Ringgold, GA 30736), or through the assessor's page on the qPublic property site.

When you file, name your path: Board of Equalization, Hearing Officer or Arbitration. The dispute may concern taxability, value or uniformity, but not the amount of tax levied. Owners of mobile homes who want a different value have 45 days to file with the assessors, then 21 days after a changed value to go to the Board of Equalization.

One common surprise: the notice estimates your tax at last year's rate. The county commissioners, the school board and the Ringgold and Fort Oglethorpe councils then work out a rollback rate, and that can bring the actual bill down.

sections.h2: Where do I apply for homestead?
sections.html:
Catoosa takes homestead applications at the tax commissioner's office, unlike counties where the assessors do. Bring a Georgia ID, and a first-time homeowner should bring the warranty deed. Applications can be submitted any time but must be received by April 1 to count for that year.

The Board of Assessors decides eligibility. If you are turned down, the office must tell you, and you can appeal. After approval the exemption renews itself until your residence, ownership or exemption type changes.

Catoosa has local exemptions that replace the state amounts when they are higher. The commissioner's website sorts them into regular, veteran and senior groups and keeps a separate page on deferral. Find out which one fits you before you choose a closing date.

Ask the tax commissioner for the full amount owed, then have the closing attorney or title company pay it from the proceeds. The commissioner's home page warns that unpaid taxes can lead to a levy and a sale, and links a Delinquent Tax Sale Information Guide and a list of excess funds from earlier sales.

Georgia attaches the lien to the property as of its January 1 valuation, ahead of other liens, which is why title companies insist on a payoff. If a tax sale notice has already arrived, phone the office that day, since timing controls your options.

  • Order the balance from the tax commissioner before you sign a contract.
  • Ask about excess-funds or tax sale notices tied to the parcel.
  • Keep the payoff letter with your closing papers.

If a bill arrives for a house you already sold, forward it to the buyer. Statements go to the owner on record, so recording the deed quickly keeps later bills from going astray.

The assessor's public notice cites O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1 and lists the reasons: a return being filed, an appeal, new construction or improvements, a records review for a property division or transfer, and a conservation use application. A visiting appraiser carries photo identification and drives a marked county vehicle. To confirm a visit, call 706-965-3772.

Georgia law requires uniform values based on the current Catoosa County sales market, and the Board of Assessors revalues every property each year. A sale or a split of a lot is the sort of change the office is likely to notice, so keep permits, survey papers and receipts for improvements within reach.

Catoosa covers 162 square miles on the Tennessee line, with Ringgold as the seat and Fort Oglethorpe as the largest city. Tunnel Hill is a town. The county belongs to the Chattanooga metropolitan area, and 76.3% of residents live in urban areas. Interstate 75 and U.S. 27 carry most of the traffic.

The 2020 census counted 67,872 people. For 2020 to 2024 the county had 26,653 households, 74.2% in owner-occupied homes, with a median owned-home value of $240,900 and a median household income of $74,639.

Order your payoff early and ask whether the parcel has any open notice of sale. Confirm which district your bill falls in so the closing agent contacts the right city, if any, for its share. Remember that your exemption ends with the sale and the buyer files on their own before April 1.

A cash sale does not change these steps, since the title company still needs the same payoff before it will release funds. If you are close to a tax sale date, call the commissioner at (706) 965-2571 before anything else.

faqs.q: Which day is the Catoosa County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: Generally December 20. One bill carries the county, Ringgold and Fort Oglethorpe taxes. The date printed on your own statement controls.

faqs.q: Can I treat a Catoosa County Notice of Assessment as my bill?
faqs.a: No. It lists the fair market value and an estimate built on last year's millage rate, and it may omit exemptions. A rollback of the rate can lower the actual bill.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for homestead in Catoosa County?
faqs.a: At the Tax Commissioner's office, with a Georgia ID and a warranty deed if you are a first-time owner. The application must be received by April 1 to count for that tax year.

faqs.q: When are Catoosa County mobile homes taxed?
faqs.a: By April 1 for homes in the county on January 1, when the location permit is issued. A late payment draws a 10% penalty, a FiFa and possibly a sale of the home.

faqs.q: Who takes a Catoosa County property appeal?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor at 798 Lafayette Street in Ringgold, in person, by mail or online. Forty-five days run from the mailing date of the notice, and you choose Board of Equalization, Hearing Officer or Arbitration when you file.
